newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian senator still wants Telstra change.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian senator still wants Telstra change.

text.p: Key Australian Independent Brian Harradine said on Wednesday he would still propose amendments to the bill for the partial sale of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp despite a lack of support from the government.

Treasurer Peter Costello late on Tuesday ruled out government support for Harradine's proposal that Telstra should be sold through redeemable preference shares, saying the financial markets would not be able to cope with such an issue.
"I'll certainly be raising it in the (upper house) Senate and I hope that colleagues will support me on it," Harradine told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
Harradine said he was unsure whether his amendment would receive support from other non-government parties.

Asked if he expected any government support for his proposal at all, Harradine said: "According to this letter (from Costello), there's not a great deal, but I believe it ought to be given a fair trial."
Harradine declined to comment on how he would vote on the bill if his amendment failed to pass, saying only that there was "a bit of water to flow under that bridge just yet".
But he said the government had treated his other concerns about the sale with consideration.
"The government, I must say, has been very considerate about the other matters that I've been dealing with," he said.
Harradine said these issues included his concerns that his home state of Tasmania should be recognised as having a pre-eminent natural heritage position and receive appropriate funding.
He was also concerned that Tasmania should not become a communications backwater and that effects on employment should be considered as part of the Telstra issue.
"On those particular matters I must say we have had some productive discussions," he said.
The government needs the support of Harradine and fellow Independent Mal Colston to pass the Telstra legislation in the non-government dominated upper house, the Senate.
All other non-government parties are opposed to the plan.
The conservative Liberal-National government plans to raise about A$8.0 billion from the sale of one-third of Telstra, with A$1.0 billion of that earmarked for an environment package.
